title: The Trail of the Coral Triangle
premise: Salvage diver Bram Montrose is hired to strip a wreck the navy refuses to acknowledge, and among the drowned cargo he finds a dying prospector clutching a map to a lost cache in the Coral Triangle's highlands. Bound by the promise he made, Bram assembles an unlikely crew — a disgraced cartographer, a runaway heiress, and the prospector's estranged daughter — and races rival salvagers and a corrupt naval officer across mountain passes before the snows seal them out. At the cache they discover not treasure but evidence of the navy's buried atrocity, and Bram must choose between wealth, silence, and truth. In the end the crew sacrifices the fortune to expose the officer, finding in each other the family none of them had.
about_author: Sebastian Ravensworth is a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade charting reefs from Indonesia to Papua New Guinea before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels steeped in salt, altitude, and the moral weather of people far from home.

chapters.title: The Wreck They Won't Name
chapters.summary: Bram Montrose's POV. Diving a forbidden wreck off the Coral Triangle coast, Bram strips brass and questions why the navy patrols it so fiercely. He finds a sealed cabin no salvage manifest explains. The beat is unease — the wilderness forgiving nothing, and Bram sensing he's already trespassing on someone's secret.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A half-drowned prospector washes into his camp, shot and dying, trading a hand-drawn map of a highland cache for Bram's word to deliver it to his daughter. The beat is reluctant honor: Bram, who trusts no one, gives his word anyway and watches the man die with the name 'Sela' on his lips.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. To read the map's ciphered margins, Bram seeks Isolde Vane, a disgraced cartographer drinking away her career in a port town. She recognizes the navy's old survey marks and agrees — for a share and a reason of her own. The beat is two damaged people striking a bargain neither fully trusts.

chapters.title: The Runaway Heiress
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. A stowaway is discovered aboard their chartered boat: Marisol Quennel, fleeing an arranged marriage and her family's shipping empire, offering money and nerve. The beat is friction becoming grudging respect as Marisol proves useful when customs officers board and search them.

chapters.title: Sela
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In a coastal village they find Sela Ardan, the prospector's estranged daughter, who hates her father and wants nothing from his map. When she learns how he died, grief cracks her anger open. The beat is mourning deferred — she joins the expedition carrying a coffin's worth of unsaid words.

chapters.title: Rivals on the Water
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Rival salvagers led by the brutal Dekker shadow their boat, and a night chase through reef channels ends with their engine sabotaged. The beat is first blood: no one dies yet, but everyone understands this is now a race with stakes beyond treasure.

chapters.title: The Officer in White
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Commander Aldous Verrick of the navy boards them under pretense of inspection, courteous and venomous, revealing he knows about the map. He lets them go — a cat playing with mice. The beat is dread; Bram realizes the wreck, the prospector's murder, and Verrick are one thread.

chapters.title: Into the Green Staircase
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The crew leaves the boats and begins the ascent through jungle terraces toward the highlands, battling leeches, rot, and Dekker's scouts behind them. The beat is endurance and bonding — Sela saves Marisol from a river crossing, and the found family starts to take shape around campfires.

chapters.title: What the Map Hides
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Deciphering the margins at last, Isolde realizes the coordinates mark not gold but a navy depot from a war nobody discusses — and that her own father surveyed it. The beat is vertigo of identity: she has spent her life escaping her father's shadow and is now walking straight into it.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. A highland village shelters them; its elders recall the depot and the men who never came home. An old woman gives Sela her father's letters, kept for decades. The beat is inherited guilt — the past is not buried here, only waiting, and the villagers ask them to carry the truth down the mountain.

chapters.title: Dekker's Bargain
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Dekker ambushes them at a rope bridge and offers to split the cache if they hand over the map. Bram stalls; Marisol bluffs him with her family's name; a scout falls to his death in the gorge. The beat is the corruption of power shown small — Dekker's crew already turning on each other.

chapters.title: The Pass Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Weather turns; they must cross the high pass within three days or be sealed out until spring — while Verrick's patrol closes from below. Frostbite, a near-fatal fall, and Isolde's collapse test them. The beat is sacrifice: Marisol burns her escape fund buying mules and passage, choosing the crew over her way home.

chapters.title: Ghosts of the Depot
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. They reach the depot ruins and find the cache: crates of documents, paymaster gold, and proof Verrick's unit massacred prisoners and sank the wreck to hide it. The beat is hollow triumph — the treasure is real, but so is the rot beneath it, and Bram sees the promise has become something larger.

chapters.title: Verrick Arrives
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Verrick's soldiers surround the depot at dusk. Calm and reasonable, he offers each of them wealth and amnesty for silence, peeling at their loyalties. Dekker's surviving crew defects to him. The beat is temptation — power dressed as generosity — and Sela spits in his face, hardening the line.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Held overnight in the depot, the crew plans in whispers. Sela reads her father's letters by candlelight and finally forgives him; Isolde confesses her father helped build the cover-up. The beat is reckoning — each character decides who they are before dawn decides for them.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Cache
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. One of Dekker's defectors frees the prisoners expecting reward, triggering chaos. Gunfire in the crates; the gold scattered; Isolde takes a bullet shielding the documents. The beat is crisis of trust — Marisol must choose between grabbing the gold that could buy her freedom and dragging Isolde clear. She chooses Isolde.

chapters.title: Flight Into the White
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. With the snows arriving early, the crew flees uphill into the storm, carrying documents instead of gold, hunted by Verrick and the defected salvagers alike. The beat is desperation transfigured — the wilderness that forgives nothing becomes their ally now, swallowing their pursuers' tracks.

chapters.title: The Avalanche
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Cornered on a cornice, Bram triggers an avalanche to bury Verrick's squad, nearly going over with it. Sela hauls him back from the edge. The beat is cost — Verrick survives but broken and exposed, and Bram learns the difference between survival and vengeance.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Wounded, feverish, Isolde is carried down-mountain as the crew navigates the thawing passes. Verrick, half his command lost, makes a final offer to Bram alone: kill the others, keep the gold. The beat is the theme made explicit — Bram refuses, because power bought with betrayal is just a fancier cage.

chapters.title: Judgment at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Reaching the coast, they broadcast the depot evidence through Marisol's family's shipping network, forcing an inquiry. Verrick is arrested as his own officers defect; Dekker vanishes with empty hands. The beat is justice without triumph — the truth costs them the fortune, and none of them regret it.

chapters.title: What We Buried, What We Kept
chapters.summary: Sela's POV. Sela buries her father's letters at the village that remembered him, at peace at last. The inquiry vindicates the dead; the crew scatters to ports and lives. The beat is release — identity no longer defined by fathers, fortunes, or flags, but by choices made on the mountain.

chapters.title: The Trail Continues
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Months later, Bram refits his boat and finds his crew waiting at the dock unasked — Isolde recovered, Marisol disowned and delighted, Sela holding a new chart. The beat is belonging: the wilderness forgets less than people do, but what this found family keeps is each other, sailing toward the next horizon.
